SMTO-HTTP-0041 — The service's sign-in system is having a problem

GUID: cb5f7f91-97d9-4bf7-8dbb-a3d197099230
Slug: http-auth-server-error
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO reached the service's sign-in address, but the service reported a fault on its own side. Changing your sign-in details won't fix this.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether the service is having an outage, for example on its status page or by signing in to its website yourself. The service reported that its own sign-in system failed.
  2. When the service is working again, open Parameter Store, select the HTTP connection, and select Test connection. Testing first confirms sign-in works before the task tries again.
  3. If the service looks healthy but the test still fails, ask its owner to check their sign-in logs for the time of this error. Only the service's owner can see why their sign-in system failed.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Authenticated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to whoever runs the service. Don't change your saved password or turn off certificate checks; neither fixes a fault on the service's side.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The authentication endpoint returned a 5xx status instead of a configured success status.

What this means

  • The authentication endpoint returned a status of 500 or greater instead of a configured success status. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The authentication endpoint returned a status of 500 or greater instead of a configured success status.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect service health and sanitized status; a proxy or upstream dependency may own the failure.

How to fix it

  • Check the authentication service's health and server logs for the failing request; local credential changes cannot repair a server-side fault. Re-test the connection once the auth endpoint returns its documented success status.
  • Inspect the authentication service health and logs. No local credential change can repair a server-side fault by itself.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended authentication route returns a valid supported success response.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
